extracted.intended_audience: prospective MacDowell fellows, artists interested in residencies, and the general public
extracted.subtask_description: Descriptive overview of MacDowell's mission, history, program features, and legacy intended to inform prospective fellows and the public about the residency experience and institutional values.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mission — nurture the arts via residential environment
rubrics_metrics.description: MacDowell's mission is to nurture the arts by offering talented individuals an inspiring residential environment in which to produce enduring works of the creative imagination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Frames the organization's purpose and what it offers fellows: time, space, and an inspiring residential setting to produce substantial creative work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expectation of producing enduring works
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide talented individuals an inspiring residential environment in which to produce enduring works of the creative imagination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The program emphasizes support for work intended to have lasting artistic value; examples of supported works (novels, compositions, plays, films, etc.) are listed as evidence of this outcome.

rubrics_metrics.name: Access to a private studio during residency
rubrics_metrics.description: Fellows have access to a private studio during residency. Set across our 450-acre property, each of the 31 studios offers its own unique personality, design, and history.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies a concrete program feature: private, individual studios on a 450-acre campus (31 studios). Useful as a practical expectation for applicants about workspace and setting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Community and peer interaction — creative excellence standard
rubrics_metrics.description: Offering them 'the opportunity to work within a dynamic community of their peers, where creative excellence is the standard.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Highlights the importance placed on community and peer exchange as part of the residency experience and positions 'creative excellence' as the program's evaluative/aspirational norm (quoted from the National Medal of Arts citation).

rubrics_metrics.name: Commitment to inclusivity — removing barriers to participation
rubrics_metrics.description: In 2020, MacDowell dropped the word 'colony' from its name to continue efforts to eliminate barriers to participation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Signals an institutional policy and value change aimed at inclusion; indicates attention to language and accessibility as part of program values.

rubrics_metrics.name: Land acknowledgement / Indigenous recognition
rubrics_metrics.description: MacDowell’s staff and board acknowledge that our residency program takes place in Wabanaki, the Dawnland, on the traditional homelands of the Western Abenaki people ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An ethical/community standard: the organization recognizes indigenous lands and signals engagement with local historical context and responsibilities (link: 'Read More').

rubrics_metrics.name: Institutional prestige and demonstrated impact
rubrics_metrics.description: MacDowell has provided time and space to more than 9,500 artists and was honored with the National Medal of Arts in 1997 for 'nurturing and inspiring many of this century’s finest artists'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Serves as evidence of the program's track record and reputation; the list of notable Fellows and supported works functions as proof of impact and standards of excellence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multilingual accessibility (Spanish translation present)
rubrics_metrics.description: The page includes Spanish-language versions of mission, history, and honors content.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicates the organization's effort to present information in at least one other language, which can be interpreted as part of accessibility/outreach practices.
